title: Hash Brown Breakfast Casserole
subtitle: A cheese, egg, hash brown, and breakfast meat bake that holds for late eaters.
description: This hall-ready hash brown breakfast casserole layers crisp-edged potatoes, eggs, cheese, and breakfast meat in a deep pan. It is built for firefighter crews whose morning meal may be interrupted, because clean squares hold better than made-to-order eggs.

ingredients.name: garlic powder
ingredients.notes: plus salt, black pepper, and paprika

steps.title: Heat oven and dry hash browns
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F and Grease a deep 9x13 baking dish. Squeeze thawed hash browns firmly in a clean towel; wet potatoes are the main reason this casserole gets a soggy bottom.

steps.title: Build the potato crust
steps.instruction: Mix hash browns with melted butter, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Press into the pan in an even layer and bake 15–18 minutes until edges begin to brown. This par-bake keeps the base from tasting boiled.

steps.title: Cook the filling
steps.instruction: Brown sausage to 165°F, or warm cooked ham, then drain well. Sauté onion until soft. Spread meat, onion, and two cups of cheese over the hot potato crust; greasy meat will make pools in the finished bake.

steps.title: Whisk and pour custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs, milk, paprika, salt, and pepper until smooth. Pour slowly over the filling, pausing to let it settle into corners. Do not stir after pouring or the potato layer will break apart.

steps.title: Bake until the center sets
steps.instruction: Bake 28–32 minutes until the center is set, reaches 165°F, and no liquid egg shakes in the middle. Add remaining cheese for the final 5 minutes. If the top browns early, tent loosely with foil.

steps.title: Rest, cut, and hold
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into 10 squares; cutting early causes loose, wet portions. Hold covered at 200°F up to 30 minutes for late eaters, then uncover for the last 5 minutes to protect the top.

stationWorkflow: Assemble the casserole the night before, cover, and refrigerate; add 10 minutes to baking time when it goes in cold.
Use a thermometer in the center, not the browned edge, to confirm the egg custard reaches 165°F.
Keep uncut squares in the warm pan during calls and cut only the portions needed for the first line.
cleanupNotes: Soak the casserole pan with hot soapy water immediately; baked potato starch and egg set hard after cooling.
Drain sausage in a lined bowl rather than down the sink to keep rendered fat out of plumbing.
leftovers: Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate up to 4 days, and reheat covered portions to 165°F.
Crisp a cold square in a skillet and top it with salsa for a quick next-shift breakfast.

adaptable.label: Dairy-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a plant-based butter/margarine. Use oat, almond, or soy milk (check tree-nut/soy status of the substitute). Use a dairy-free cheese shred/block alternative.

adaptable.label: Pork-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Swap in chicken or turkey sausage.
